literal: Yet idle posts are examined on many years while arduous posts are graded on few years—above it violates the evenness of Heaven's favor, below it breeds the suffering of inequality.
idiomatic: Idle posts are judged on long years while arduous posts on short ones—above, Heaven's favor is uneven; below, men suffer unequal hardship.

literal: Moreover, in the regulations of the Jingming era there is no text on reduced examination;
idiomatic: The Jingming regulations contain no rule for reduced examination;

literal: the memorial of the Zhengshi era had grades of grant and strip.
idiomatic: the Zhengshi memorial had grades of grant and strip.

literal: Clearly uneven examination is not the mind of sagely compassion;
idiomatic: Uneven examination is not sagely compassion;

literal: to change the canon and alter the constant is the intent of the responsible offices.
idiomatic: changing canon and custom is the clerks' doing.

literal: Moreover, in seeking the memorial on examination grades, it is entrusted to the hands of active officers;
idiomatic: Examination grades are left in active officers' hands;

literal: those touching deliberation on merit and diligence are cut off from the brush of scattered officers.
idiomatic: merit and diligence never reach scattered officers' pens.

literal: Thus those in office can display their own diligent ability, while the scattered cohort alone is denied a place to open the breast.
idiomatic: Men in office can show diligence; scattered officers alone have no place to plead their case.

literal: Suppressing the gap between upper and lower, bounded by the judgment of edict regulations, it causes those in close attendance and forbidden offices to hold words of bent dish and bowed knee;
idiomatic: Edict rules bound upper and lower so close attendants and forbidden offices must speak with bent dish and bowed knee;

literal: guards and martial men harbor resentment that cannot be voiced.
idiomatic: palace guards and martial men nurse unvoiced resentment.

literal: Wishing to level the four seas—how will you win them?
idiomatic: If you wish to pacify the four seas, how will you win men's hearts?

literal: Moreover, scattered officers on duty: one stain becomes a fault;
idiomatic: A scattered officer on duty: one stain becomes guilt;

literal: bearing an envoy commission, a slip becomes punishment seated.
idiomatic: on envoy service, a hair's breadth of error brings punishment.

literal: What fine cords seize them is not eased because the matter is light;
idiomatic: The fine net of law does not ease because the fault is small;

literal: festival gifts are not increased because the stipend is slight.
idiomatic: festival gifts are not enlarged because the stipend is slight.

literal: Palace offenses are not distinguished from active office;
idiomatic: palace offenses are not treated differently from active office;

literal: the mechanism of examination and promotion pushes years unequally.
idiomatic: promotion by years falls unequally.

literal: I have heard that what the lord raises must be written; if written and not lawful, what will later generations look upon?
idiomatic: What the lord does must be written; if the record is unlawful, what will posterity see?

literal: The Odes say: "The king's affairs never rest, no leisure to rise or sit," and also: "Do we not long for home? We fear these brief letters."
idiomatic: The Odes say: "Kingly tasks never cease—no time to rise or sit," and: "Do we not yearn for home? We fear the dispatch."

literal: The yielding willows tell of levying troops for war;
idiomatic: Yielding willows speak of mustering troops;

literal: the drizzling snow again declares the toil of rousing the army.
idiomatic: drizzling snow declares the army's toil anew.

literal: If coming and going days are reduced, then the poem of gathering fern is abandoned and the song of the lone pear tree ends.
idiomatic: If days of coming and going are cut, the poem of gathering fern is silenced and the song of the lone pear tree ends.

literal: Moreover, officers in active office, for fortune and misfortune, leave and mourning, fixed visits and tomb-sweeping, often run ten ten-day periods; sometimes because of grave illness they request leave, often stretching to a full year.
idiomatic: Active officers take leave for fortune, mourning, visits, and tomb-sweeping for ten-day spans at a stretch, sometimes a year for grave illness.

literal: On campaign on the road, diligence is a hundredfold.
idiomatic: On campaign, diligence is a hundredfold harder.

literal: The posture of bitterness and joy is not of the same kind as active office;
idiomatic: Bitterness and joy do not match active office;

literal: private leisure at home is not a day of governing affairs.
idiomatic: private leisure at home is not a day of public duty.

literal: In speaking of merit and discussing arduous service, the active should first be reduced.
idiomatic: When weighing merit and hardship, active officers should be judged first.

literal: Military men originally rated at the top grade became Forest of Feathers guards, those at the next grade became Tiger Guards, those at the lowest became direct followers.
idiomatic: Top-rated soldiers entered the Forest of Feathers, the next grade the Tiger Guards, the lowest direct followers.

literal: Some for accumulated years on campaign garrisoned everywhere without exception;
idiomatic: Some campaigned year on year and garrisoned every frontier;

literal: some in armor year after year bore a thousand li;
idiomatic: some bore armor year after year for a thousand li;

literal: some were wounded in battle;
idiomatic: some were battle-wounded;

literal: some aged and failed.
idiomatic: some aged and failed.

literal: Now they are tested against their original grade and required to be as at first; where they fall short of before, ranks are reduced and grades stripped.
idiomatic: Now they are tested against their first rating and must match it; falling short, rank and grade are stripped.

literal: This demands that they not decline—reason does not pass through.
idiomatic: To demand they never decline is unreasonable.

literal: Moreover, envoys to border peoples must draw court elites.
idiomatic: Envoys to border peoples must draw court elites.

literal: Some crossed a thousand li of peril, some trod ten thousand li of danger; ascending they had the worry of death, all harbored the grief of not returning—soul and bone offered loyalty, presenting the corpse in place of life.
idiomatic: Some crossed a thousand li of peril or ten thousand li of danger, facing death and the grief of never returning—offering soul and bone, they would present their corpse in the place of life.

literal: The former court's reward scale repaid with noble rank;
idiomatic: The former court repaid them with noble rank;

literal: the present court changes the form and stops at grade and toil.
idiomatic: the present court changes the form and stops at grade and toil.

literal: Reducing it to replace examination violates the envoy's hope.
idiomatic: Reducing reward to examination violates what envoys hoped for.

literal: It is not the means to encourage the splendid envoys and honor the four stalwart steeds.
idiomatic: It is no way to encourage splendid envoys or honor the four stalwart steeds.

literal: I again seek the regulations of Zhengshi: broadly, those afterward in active office rated upper-middle advance one grade in three years;
idiomatic: I turn again to Zhengshi regulations: broadly, later active officers rated upper-middle rose one grade in three years;

literal: broadly, those before in active office rated upper-middle advance one rank in six years.
idiomatic: earlier active officers rated upper-middle rose one rank in six years.

literal: Examination every three years is the universal classic since antiquity.
idiomatic: Triennial examination is the universal classic since antiquity.

literal: Now with six years before the broad advance of one grade, if no fault is found, doubling years completes the rank.
idiomatic: Now six years broadly earn one grade without fault—doubled years complete a rank.

literal: Pushing from this, clearly the broad replaces examination.
idiomatic: From this it is clear that breadth replaces examination.

literal: On the first day of new appointment all alike touch grade glory; those of lower grade rise by breadth, while men of upper grade fall by breadth.
idiomatic: On the first day of appointment all share grade glory; lower men rise by breadth while upper men fall.

literal: I also see that the qualification grade of section and commandant originally stood outside the flowing ranks; it was published in bright edicts and practiced long.
idiomatic: Section and commandant qualification grades originally stood outside the flowing ranks, set forth in bright edicts and long practiced.

literal: Yet recently in lanes and alleys thieves are many; because their authority is light and does not awe, they wish to advance the grade into the clear current to press down treachery and villainy.
idiomatic: Yet lanes swarm with thieves; because section authority is too light to awe them, some wish to raise the grade into the clear current to crush crime.

literal: Zhen Chen memorialized:[15] "For one who makes law, enact it and observe; if inconvenient, then change."
idiomatic: Zhen Chen wrote:[15] "Enact law and watch it; if it fails, change it."

literal: I venture that this saying may be adopted; let sagely compassion scan it and further raise the rank of the higher commandants.
idiomatic: That saying deserves adoption; let sagely compassion scan it and raise the higher commandants' rank.

literal: Now as the examination regulations are first proclaimed, those who harbor resentment are many; I have observed it in private and also say it cannot stand; it has light on the national canon—how hard is it to change?
idiomatic: The new examination rules breed widespread resentment; I have watched in private and judge them untenable; they touch the national canon—how hard is change?

literal: Shizong thereupon summoned Yong to discuss current affairs together.
idiomatic: Shizong then summoned Yong to discuss current affairs.

literal: At the beginning of Suzong's reign an edict ordered Yong to enter and dwell in the Western Cypress Hall of the Great Ultimate, to consult and decide great government, with twenty trusted attendants granted.
idiomatic: Early in Suzong's reign Yong was ordered into the Western Cypress Hall of the Great Ultimate to decide great affairs, with twenty trusted attendants.

literal: An edict also made Yong Imperial Clan Mentor, advanced to Grand Tutor and Palace Attendant, holding Duke of the Martial Host concurrently, prince as before.
idiomatic: He was also named imperial clan mentor, grand tutor, palace attendant, and duke of the martial host, prince unchanged.

literal: A separate edict ordered the Director of Imperial Construction to build the National University temple and grant it for Yong's residence.
idiomatic: A separate edict had the director of imperial construction build the National University temple for Yong's residence.

literal: Army Supervisor Yu Zhong seized power and acted willfully; Vice Director Guo Zuo urged Yong to remove him.
idiomatic: Army supervisor Yu Zhong seized power willfully; vice director Guo Zuo urged Yong to remove him.

literal: Zhong was enraged, forged an edict to kill Zuo and Minister Pei Zhi, and deposed Yong to return to his residence as prince.
idiomatic: Zhong forged an edict, killed Zuo and Minister Pei Zhi, and deposed Yong to his princely residence.

literal: When the court had great affairs, a Yellow Gate gentleman was sent to consult him.
idiomatic: On great court affairs a yellow gate gentleman was sent to consult him.

literal: Before long Zhong again forged an edict and was about to kill Yong; he asked Palace Attendant Cui Guang, who refused—thereupon he stopped.
idiomatic: Soon Zhong forged again to kill Yong and asked Palace Attendant Cui Guang, who refused, and he stopped.

literal: Before long Empress Dowager Ling took the court; Zhong was sent out as Inspector of Ji Province.
idiomatic: Soon Empress Dowager Ling ruled; Zhong was sent out as Jizhou inspector.

literal: Yong memorialized:
idiomatic: Yong memorialized:

literal: When I first entered the Cypress Hall I saw that the issuing of edicts all passed through the Gate Office, yet I went out while the lord acted and did not change my mind.
idiomatic: When I entered the Cypress Hall I saw edicts issue only through the Gate Office, yet I went out while the lord acted and did not change course.

literal: Each time I read it I was wounded and pained; each time I looked it was a bitter sight; I knew deeply it could not stand yet could not forbid it.
idiomatic: Each reading wounded me; each sight was bitter; I knew it could not stand yet could not stop it.

literal: My first offense.
idiomatic: My first offense.

literal: I have recently been shamed to hold the inner pivot and concurrently bear the mentor's corpse, and should protect the sacred person, warm and cool morning and evening.
idiomatic: I lately hold the inner pivot and the mentor's charge and should protect the sacred person morning and evening.

literal: Yet Yu Zhong holds the martial office and controls restraint at will; bounded within and without, court audience is cut off.
idiomatic: Yet Yu Zhong holds the martial office and controls restraint at will; inside and outside, audience is cut off.

literal: Where the imperial dwelling sleeps and eats is unknown; the altars' safety is also not foreseen; entering and leaving the Cypress Hall, standing corpse only.
idiomatic: Where the emperor sleeps and eats is unknown; the altars' safety unforeseeable; I enter and leave the Cypress Hall a standing corpse only.

literal: My second offense.
idiomatic: My second offense.

literal: Zhong plotted to kill me, relying on those in office who held him off.
idiomatic: Zhong plotted my death, stopped only by men in office who held him off.

literal: He also ordered vice directors and ministers to advance and dismiss at will; transfer of office and grant of post often did not pass ten days; worthy men were driven off and heart-followers alone received—his might shook the hundred offices, his power tilted court and realm.
idiomatic: He made vice directors and ministers advance and dismiss at will, often within ten days, driving off the worthy and taking heart-followers—his might shook the hundred offices, his power tilted the realm.

literal: Seeing him thus, I wished to send Zhong out as Inspector of Yong Province to pacify and settle Guanxi; in heart I had not acted when in turn Zhong deposed me.
idiomatic: Seeing this, I wished to send him out as Yongzhou inspector to settle Guanxi; I had not acted when he deposed me in turn.

literal: Shamed in office, corpse in stipend, alone I failed private favor.
idiomatic: Shamed in office, corpse in stipend, I failed private favor alone.

literal: My third offense.
idiomatic: My third offense.

literal: When the late emperor ascended to the far journey the heir apparent succeeded the line—this is the constant plan of lord and father and the eternal rule of subject and son; the meaning of added reward has from antiquity been without precedent.
idiomatic: When the late emperor died the heir succeeded—lord-and-father's constant plan, subject-and-son's eternal rule; added reward has no ancient precedent.

literal: Zhong was already a subject, receiving favor from the late emperor; at the moment of mourning calamity exhausting integrity was the constant—welcoming Your Majesty at the Eastern Palace was subjects' constant affair; if not that, what more was there to do?
idiomatic: Zhong was the late emperor's favored subject; at mourning, exhausting loyalty was constant—welcoming Your Majesty at the Eastern Palace was every subject's duty; what more was required?

literal: Yet Zhong's spirit and air pierced the clouds; sitting he demanded enfeoffment.
idiomatic: Yet Zhong's spirit pierced the clouds and he demanded enfeoffment while seated.

literal: That day if suppressed, in turn I feared it would become calamity.
idiomatic: That day to suppress him might bring calamity in turn.

literal: Because the powerful minister desired it, I did not dare lightly oppose; I at once gathered kings, dukes, and gentlemen to deliberate the amount.
idiomatic: Because the powerful minister desired it I did not dare oppose; I gathered kings, dukes, and gentlemen to fix the amount.

literal: Prince of Qinghe, my lord Yi, the late emperor's honored younger brother, with broad measure and clear insight, facing the crowd led the deliberation—not because of diligence that he rewarded, but fearing to violate the powerful minister's intent, looking at his face and granting.
idiomatic: Prince Qinghe Yi, the late emperor's honored brother, clear and broad, led the crowd—not rewarding merit but fearing the powerful minister, granting as his face commanded.

literal: I knew it could not stand and therefore followed.
idiomatic: I knew it could not stand and followed.

literal: My fourth offense.
idiomatic: My fourth offense.

literal: Zhong held power at the Gate Office and also sat as chief minister, and again held overall command of the forbidden guard, as Commandant of Chongxun and Guard—body holding inner and outer, crossing into the palace apartments.
idiomatic: Zhong held the Gate Office and the chief ministry, commanded the forbidden guard, was commandant of Chongxun and guard—inner and outer in one body, crossing the palace.

literal: My fifth offense.
idiomatic: My fifth offense.

literal: In antiquity for heavy crimes the three dukes had to assemble; the term reached ten days—therefore capital punishment was weighted.
idiomatic: In antiquity heavy crimes required the three dukes to assemble for ten days—therefore capital punishment was weighted.

literal: When the late emperor ascended the throne, seventeen years; petty men who violated punishment still had lenient ink of the statutes; court nobles in office—not one was executed.
idiomatic: Seventeen years the late emperor reigned; petty offenders still met lenient statutes; not one court noble was executed.

literal: Now Your Majesty has trodden the throne not yet half a cycle and killed Vice Director and Minister like plucking a single blade of grass in its prime—this is Zhong seizing power by forged edict and willfully carrying out execution.
idiomatic: Your Majesty has reigned less than half a year and killed vice director and minister like plucking spring grass—Zhong forged edicts and killed at will.

literal: I knew I could not save them—my sixth offense.
idiomatic: I knew I could not save them—my sixth offense.

literal: My post bears mentor and minister; my years have not reached the end; unpardonable offenses, manifest not one—what feeling to dwell, what face to live? Though grace has pardoned, still there is remaining blame; I respectfully return to my private gate and await the office of punishment.
idiomatic: I bear mentor and minister though my years are not ended; unpardonable offenses stand manifest—what feeling to dwell, what face to live? Though grace pardons, blame remains; I return to my private gate and await punishment.

literal: Empress Dowager Ling was moved by Zhong's merit in protection and did not question his crimes; Yong's fief was increased by one thousand households, he was made Palace Attendant and Grand Mentor, and Bearer of the Staff was added to lead his former office as Governor of Si Province.
idiomatic: Empress Dowager Ling, moved by Zhong's protective merit, did not punish him; Yong's fief rose a thousand households, he was palace attendant and grand mentor, bearer of the staff added, leading Si province as before.

literal: Yong memorialized requesting: from kings and dukes down, concubines may not use woven brocade, gold, jade, pearls, or gems—violators judged by violation of edict;
idiomatic: Yong asked that from kings and dukes down concubines might not use brocade, gold, jade, pearls, or gems—violators judged by edict violation;

literal: slave girls may not wear gauze damask or patterned silk, stopping at plain silk only; male slaves plain cloth, and none may use gold or silver for hairpins and belts—violators flogged one hundred.
idiomatic: slave girls only plain silk, male slaves plain cloth, no gold or silver pins or belts—violators flogged a hundred.

literal: The empress dowager followed it, yet could not enforce it long.
idiomatic: The empress dowager agreed but could not enforce it long.

literal: An edict ordered Yong to ride a step-drawn carriage in and out of the side gate.
idiomatic: An edict let Yong ride a step-drawn carriage through the side gate.

literal: He was again Recorder of the Masters of Writing in his former office.
idiomatic: He was again recorder of the Masters of Writing in his former office.

literal: Yong repeatedly memorialized to decline; gracious replies did not permit it; an edict ordered a palace attendant to press the instruction.
idiomatic: Yong repeatedly declined; gracious replies refused; a palace attendant was ordered to press him.

literal: An edict ordered Yong to attend and lecture morning and evening.
idiomatic: An edict ordered Yong to lecture morning and evening.

literal: When Suzong took charge of government he was made Bearer of the Staff, Governor of Si Province, Palace Attendant, Grand Mentor, and Recorder of the Masters of Writing as before.
idiomatic: When Suzong assumed government he was bearer of the staff, Si province governor, palace attendant, grand mentor, recorder unchanged.

literal: When Suzong received the capping rite, Yong concurrently held Grand Mentor and with Concurrent Grand Martial Host Cui Guang performed the capping rite in proxy.
idiomatic: At Suzong's capping Yong was concurrent grand mentor and with concurrent grand martial host Cui Guang performed the rite in proxy.

literal: An edict ordered Yong to ride a carriage in and out of the Great Marshal Gate, advanced to Chancellor, granted feather-canopy, drums, and pipes, doubled ceremonial swords—all else as before.
idiomatic: An edict let Yong ride through the Great Marshal Gate, advanced him to chancellor, granted feather-canopy escort, drums, pipes, and doubled ceremonial swords—all else unchanged.

literal: He was also granted eight hundred bolts of silk and supplies for a thousand men, urged to accept speedily.
idiomatic: He was also granted eight hundred bolts of silk and supplies for a thousand men, urged to accept at once.
